title: [Spec] Add +0/+1/+2/+3/+4 opponent successful-bid bonuses across Antes 1–5
body:
## Approved decision

Use **successful-bid bonuses only** for opponent scaling. Both teams start every match at **0 points**; do not add a starting-score advantage.

When the opponent team successfully makes its bid, award one additional team-score bonus according to the current ante:

| Ante | Successful opponent bid bonus |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | +0 points |
| 2 | +1 point |
| 3 | +2 points |
| 4 | +3 points |
| 5 | +4 points |

The user explicitly confirmed these values and zero starting scores. This applies across the campaign's matches in Antes 1–5, including bosses. It is a points bonus for making the contract, not money or a bonus for each individual trick. Failed opponent bids and bids made by the player's team receive no bonus from this rule.

## Current behavior

Both teams already start at zero. Successful opposing bids currently receive no ante-dependent bonus, so the score-settlement path needs the ante's approved bonus.

Related: #23 covers separate boss-rule design; this decision does not introduce boss starting-score advantages. #67 covers the updated ante targets.

**Alpha: You can outbid your partner by matching any bid you have unlocked, including Partner's Best and Alone.**

The user confirmed that matching is not limited to numeric bids. Alpha permits matching the partner's leading bid while preserving the bid's unlock requirements and other eligibility rules. It does not permit matching an opponent's bid.

The audited matching exception requires `bid <= BidLevel.Six`, so it rejects matching Partner's Best and Alone even when unlocked. The separate bid-2 path also requires the current high bid to be below 2; it must be included when enforcing the approved “any unlocked bid” rule.

The audit's targeted runtime probe confirmed matching Six succeeds while matching Partner's Best and Alone fails. Implementation changes are required.

title: [Idea] Let players close unwanted tables from the web lobby
body:
## Opportunity
The web server now has a bounded session pool (32 tables by default), but the lobby only opens tables and creates new ones. It offers no way to remove abandoned/completed tables, even though the server already exposes `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}`.

At the limit, users must wait for idle expiry (30 minutes by default), restart the server, or issue an API request themselves. This is distinct from #21, which added the server-side resource bounds, and #29, which proposes rematches.

## Proposal
Add a Close table action to each lobby card and/or the table header. Confirm closing an active game with the table's name and state, then use the existing deletion endpoint, refresh the list, and announce success or failure. Make Open and Close separate semantic controls so the actions do not interfere.

## Acceptance criteria
- A table can be closed without restarting the server or using developer tools.
- Closing releases bot resources via the existing session removal path and immediately frees a capacity slot.
- A failed deletion leaves the card available with a clear error; deleting the currently viewed table returns to the lobby.
- Keyboard and screen-reader users can operate the action.

Evidence: [lobby rendering](https://github.com/MrMortem/bidEuchre/blob/6c657d57f93ad31aa8259cb67bca78daf1af7fb3/src/BidEuchre.Server/wwwroot/app.js#L149), [existing deletion endpoint](https://github.com/MrMortem/bidEuchre/blob/6c657d57f93ad31aa8259cb67bca78daf1af7fb3/src/BidEuchre.Server/Program.cs#L122), and README's documented capacity/expiry. Feature proposal from the 2026-11-13 audit; no implementation change made.

title: Shop: reroll, clearer full-slot state, and locked offers
body:
Observations from the shop screen:

- The shop offers two Jokers even when all five Joker slots are full; pressing Buy just fails with "Five Joker slots; no duplicates." There is no hint on the card that it cannot be bought until a Joker is sold.
- The same for Tarots/Sigils when the four item slots are full (only "Buy & Use" works).
- Offers are fixed per visit. With money left over (interest caps at $5 for $25 held) there is nothing to spend it on.
- Bot seats accumulate "generated" Tarots they can never use, which is invisible to the player.

## Proposal
- **Reroll** button with an escalating price ($2, +$1 per reroll, reset each shop), using the saved campaign RNG so it stays deterministic.
- Grey out / badge offers that cannot be bought right now and say why ("Sell a Joker first", "Not enough money").
- Optional: lock an offer to keep it for the next shop; a small chance of a discounted or rare offer.
- Show the sell value on owned Jokers before pressing them.

title: Smarter built-in TableBot for free play
body:
`BuiltInBotDriver` (`src/BidEuchre.App/BotDrivers.cs`) is the default for every bot seat:

- Bids only `3`, only when nobody has bid yet and it holds three cards of a suit (it counts every Jack towards every suit). It never raises, and never bids Partners Best or Alone.
- Always names a trump suit; never High or Low.
- Always plays its highest-rank legal card (lowest in Low) – it overtakes its own partner's winning trick and treats a 9 of trump as weaker than an off-suit Ace.

The repository already contains much stronger engines (`engines/cpp-heuristic`, `engines/hybrid`, `engines/python-cfr`, `engines/prolog`), but a new player gets TableBot unless they find the Engines page and load an executable by path.

## Proposal
- Port a reasonable heuristic into the built-in driver: hand evaluation per contract, raise logic, partner awareness, trump management, lowest winning card.
- Or ship the C++ heuristic with the app and make it the default, with TableBot as "Easy".
- A difficulty choice on the New Session page.

title: Resume an unfinished campaign match instead of forfeiting it
body:
## Current behaviour
Closing the app (or a crash) during a campaign match counts as a loss: `CampaignFlow.Resume` calls `saved.Forfeit()` for a save in `InMatch`, costing 1–2 of 3 lives. The only warning is the two-step "Forfeit match?" menu button; closing the window gives none.

## Proposal
The run is already checkpointed after every action (`CampaignFlow.Checkpoint`), and the campaign RNG state is part of the snapshot. Persist the match itself as well – scores, hand number, dealer, hands, auction, current trick, per-hand effect counters, overlays – so "Continue" puts the player back at the table.

Smaller steps that would already help:
- Save at hand boundaries and resume from the start of the current hand.
- Ask for confirmation when the window is closed during a match.

title: Show a hand summary and event log: score changes are currently unexplained
body:
## Problem
The engine records exactly what happened in `GameView.Events` and `HandHistory` (bids, each effect: "Effect 3: Lucky +4 points for team 2", the per-team breakdown "contract −4; cards +9; Jokers +3; trick multipliers +1; hand ×2"). The desktop client never displays either of them.

When a hand ends the table only shows "Hand complete" and a "Deal next hand" button. In one audited campaign hand the score went from 0–0 to −8 / +18 on a failed bid of 4 with no explanation on screen. With Jokers, enhancements, Sigils and Chaos doubling in play, the player cannot learn what their build is doing.

## Suggested
- A hand-result panel: contract, made/set, tricks, and the per-team breakdown (contract / cards / Jokers / multipliers / ×factor) – the data is already in the events.
- A scrollable log (or toasts next to the card/Joker that fired) for effects during the hand, including money gained.
- A match-end screen for free play with the final score and hand-by-hand history.
